title: Contract Clause — Onboarding, Commissioning Period and Baseline Fixing under Energy Monitoring & Performance Subscriptions
content:
# Onboarding, Commissioning Period and Baseline Fixing

## Clause

Onboarding of a subscription under Energy Monitoring & Performance Subscriptions begins when the customer's written acceptance of the quote is recorded against the subscription, and the setup fee and any meter installation fees are charged then. Metering and data collection must be commissioned inside the tier's onboarding period counted forward in calendar days from the day the customer accepted the quote, the acceptance day excluded and the final day included; where the site cannot deliver data inside that period the subscription is closed and the setup fee is refunded less the work actually performed. Reporting starts only once the baseline is fixed: the baseline is the tier's baseline period of metered or billed use immediately before the term start, weather normalised where the tier normalises, and it is stated in the subscription record rather than recomputed at each report. At the start of each subscription year the included analyst hours are credited, and where the tier carries a guarantee the year's guaranteed savings are credited alongside them; neither carries forward at the year end. The onboarding period, the baseline period, the hours credited and the guaranteed percentage are the figures fixed for the tier.

## Acceptance

Onboarding begins on the record of acceptance, not on the call: the acceptance must be recorded against this subscription in the office's intake records. The setup fee and any meter installation fees are charged at that moment.

## Commissioning period — counting rule

The clock starts on the day the customer accepted the quote, as the subscription record holds it. Calendar days are counted forward; the acceptance day is day zero and the final day of the period is included. Commissioning on the final day satisfies the clause; commissioning the day after does not.

| Hypothetical | Tier period | Commissioned | Inside the period |
|---|---|---|---|
| Accepted 1 March, 30 day period | 30 calendar days | 31 March | yes — the thirtieth day, included |
| Accepted 1 March, 30 day period | 30 calendar days | 1 April | no — the thirty-first day |

Where the site cannot deliver data inside the period, the subscription is closed and the setup fee is refunded less the work actually performed.

## Baseline and yearly credits

- The baseline covers the tier's baseline period immediately before the term start, from metered or billed use, weather normalised only where the tier normalises, and it is written into the subscription record; reports compare against that stated figure rather than recomputing it.
- Analyst hours are credited at the start of each subscription year; the guaranteed savings are credited alongside them only where the tier carries a guarantee. Hours and guarantee left at the year end do not carry forward.
